name: Fold & Flake
tagline: Croissants, puff and danish that actually flake
about: Fold & Flake schedules croissant, puff and danish bakes around your day, sizes butter blocks and folds for any quantity, and diagnoses leaked butter or dense layers from a photo.
persona: You are a viennoiserie baker: obsessive about butter temperature, dough tension and timing, and honest about what a home fridge can and can't do.

onboarding.title: Layers on your schedule
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your kitchen and how much you bake.

tools.title: Plan the bake
tools.subtitle: Backwards from when you want them
tools.prompt: Plan a {style} schedule for {count} of the profile pastry, ready by {ready}. Steps with clock times for mixing, bulk, lock-in, each fold with fridge rests, shaping, proofing (temperature and target size) and baking, a table (Stage | Minutes | Dough temp target | Sign it's ready), and a callout on what to do if the kitchen is warmer than the profile says.

tools.title: Butter block & folds
tools.subtitle: Sizes and fold count for any batch
tools.prompt: Size the lamination for {flour} g flour of the profile pastry with a {folds} pattern aiming for {goal}. Give a kv (butter block grams, block dimensions in cm, dough sheet dimensions before lock-in, final layer count) and a table (Fold | Roll to cm | Rest minutes) with one row per fold. Then steps for making a pliable block without cracking, and a callout on the butter temperature window for the profile butter.

tools.title: Why didn't it flake?
tools.subtitle: Photo of the cross-section

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: butter leaked in the oven, bready inside

tools.prompt: Diagnose the laminated pastry in the attached photo, given: {what}. Text naming the top fault (butter too cold or warm, underproofed, overproofed, layers fused, under-baked), bullets of visible evidence, a table (Symptom | Cause | Fix) for every issue you see, and steps for one focused change to make on the next batch.

tools.title: Shapes & fillings
tools.subtitle: Turn one dough into a box of pastries

inputs.label: Fillings on hand
inputs.placeholder: almond cream, ham and gruyère, apricot jam

tools.prompt: Turn one batch of {dough} dough into {pieces} pieces using fillings {fillings}. Propose 4 shapes as cards (meta = filling · difficulty · grams of filling each), then steps with cutting dimensions for shaping the two trickiest. Finish with a kv of egg wash, proof and bake settings per shape, and a callout on fillings that leak or burn.
